html:
The Lower Pima, or Pima Bajo, who call themselves O'ob, are an Indigenous people of the Sierra Madre foothills and river valleys of central Sonora and western Chihuahua, Mexico. They are the southern branch of the O'odham peoples, and their language is close to those of the Akimel O'odham and Tohono O'odham further north.

They farmed maize, beans and squash along rivers such as the Yaqui. Jesuit missionaries arrived in the early 1600s and gathered them into mission towns such as Ónavas, as they did with their neighbours the Yaqui and the Eudeve. Many Lower Pima were later absorbed into the mestizo population. A small community remains today, mostly in the mountains around Yécora and Maycoba.
